summary: 제안 논문은 기존 논문의 자기지도 사전학습 틀을 유지하면서 MLM, NSP, 입력 형식, 어휘 체계 등 구체적 사전학습 구성요소와 학습 절차를 재검증·변형한 후속 연구이다. 두 논문은 Transformer 인코더 기반 표현을 만들어 GLUE와 SQuAD 같은 하위 과제에 미세조정한다는 공통 범위를 가지지만, 제안 논문은 NSP 제거, dynamic masking, FULL-SENTENCES, larger byte-level BPE, 추가 데이터와 같은 설계 선택을 통해 기존 논문을 확장한다.

caution_points: [M2 ↔ P2] NSP objective removal can be pointed out as a direct modification of the prior work's next sentence prediction task, so the manuscript should clarify that the contribution is the empirical re-evaluation of this objective within a revised pretraining procedure rather than the introduction of sentence-level relation modeling itself.

[M4 ↔ P1] Dynamic masking may be criticized as a variant of the prior work's masked language model objective, so the manuscript should state that the difference lies in changing the masking pattern during training and explain why that procedural change matters for pretraining behavior.

[M5 ↔ P1] Dynamic masking shares the same MLM objective with the prior work, so the manuscript should distinguish the work by describing the training-time masking policy and its role in reducing reliance on a fixed corruption pattern.

[M6 ↔ P2,P5,P6,P8] FULL-SENTENCES without NSP loss can be viewed as a redesign of the prior work's sentence-pair objective and input construction, so the manuscript should specify how the training input composition differs from the prior work and why removing NSP changes the pretraining setup.

[M8 ↔ P6] A larger byte-level BPE can be criticized as a replacement for the prior work's WordPiece embeddings, so the manuscript should make clear that the contribution is the changed vocabulary design and tokenization granularity rather than the general use of subword input representations.

[R-M1 ↔ R-P11] Both papers report SQuAD v1.1 dev single EM under the same condition, so reviewers can directly compare the numbers; the manuscript should explain that the comparison reflects changed training procedure and design choices within a shared evaluation setting.

[R-M2 ↔ R-P12] Both papers report SQuAD v1.1 dev single F1 under the same condition, so reviewers can make a direct result comparison; the manuscript should explicitly tie the difference in scores to altered pretraining choices rather than to a changed evaluation setup.

[R-M3 ↔ R-P23] Both papers report SQuAD v2.0 dev single EM under the same condition, so reviewers can directly compare the numbers; the manuscript should emphasize that the evaluation setting is shared while the pretraining procedure is revised.

[R-M4 ↔ R-P24] Both papers report SQuAD v2.0 dev single F1 under the same condition, so reviewers can directly compare the results; the manuscript should attribute the difference to revised pretraining design choices within the same downstream evaluation setup.

[R-M5 ↔ R-P25] Both papers report SQuAD v2.0 test single EM under the same condition, so reviewers can directly compare the numbers; the manuscript should explain that the comparison is enabled by shared evaluation conditions and that the distinction comes from the training procedure.

[R-M6 ↔ R-P26] Both papers report SQuAD v2.0 test single F1 under the same condition, so reviewers can directly compare the numbers; the manuscript should connect that comparison to the altered masking, sentence objective, and training setup.
differentiation_suggestions: Our work removes the next sentence prediction objective and re-examines pretraining under a setup that focuses on alternative design choices rather than retaining the prior sentence-pair classification objective. This difference should be stated as a change in the pretraining objective and training procedure, not as a change in the downstream fine-tuning framework.

Our work keeps the masked language modeling framework but changes the masking pattern dynamically during training. The manuscript can describe this as a procedural difference from the prior work's MLM setup, where the objective family is shared but the corruption schedule is changed.

Our work uses a larger byte-level BPE vocabulary, whereas the prior work uses WordPiece embeddings. The manuscript can present this as a concrete difference in input representation design and tokenization granularity within a broadly similar Transformer encoder pretraining framework.
related_work_draft: The prior work (Devlin et al., arXiv, 2019) introduced BERT with masked language modeling, next sentence prediction, and a bidirectional Transformer encoder for language understanding. Our work follows the same general pretraining-and-fine-tuning paradigm while revisiting several of those design choices, including the sentence objective, masking strategy, and input vocabulary.

differentiation_suggestions: Our work removes the next sentence prediction objective and evaluates pretraining under a FULL-SENTENCES input setting, whereas the prior work includes next sentence prediction as part of pretraining. The manuscript should explicitly explain how this change alters the training procedure rather than only the model family.

Our work keeps masked language modeling but changes how masks are applied by dynamically varying the masking pattern during training. This distinction should be described as a procedural change within the same self-supervised objective, not as a completely different pretraining target.

Our work also extends the data and tokenization conditions by using a larger byte-level BPE vocabulary and an additional CC-NEWS dataset. These differences should be stated as changes in input representation and data scope relative to the prior work.
related_work_draft: The prior work (Devlin et al., arXiv, 2019) introduced BERT pre-training with masked language modeling and next sentence prediction in a bidirectional Transformer encoder. Our work follows the same pretraining framework but revisits several design choices and training procedures, including masking strategy, sentence-level objective, vocabulary, and data scale.

differentiation_suggestions: Our work removes the next sentence prediction objective and reconsiders the pretraining setup without that auxiliary loss. This difference should be described as a change in training procedure rather than as a new pretraining objective family.

Our work keeps masked language model pretraining but dynamically changes the masking pattern applied to the training data. This makes the distinction from the prior work a procedural change in how masking is applied during pretraining.

Our work uses a larger byte-level BPE and adds the CC-NEWS dataset, which changes the vocabulary construction and data scope used during pretraining. This difference should be framed in terms of input representation and pretraining data range.
related_work_draft: The prior work (Devlin et al., arXiv, 2019) introduced BERT with masked language modeling and next sentence prediction for bidirectional pre-training. Our work revisits the same pretraining framework while modifying design choices such as dynamic masking, removal of next sentence prediction, and pretraining data scale.
